text:
A power station of about 1,000 Wh is enough to run one heated blanket all night. Two of the picks below fit that size.

**Top pick: BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 (1,024 Wh).** [Blackoutwise's top pick for electric blankets](https://www.blackoutwise.com/best/best-power-station-for-electric-blanket) says it runs a 150 W blanket for about 12 hours, which covers an 8-hour night with some left over. It usually sells for about $380 to $500 and weighs 25 lb. If you want two nights without recharging, the same source says the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 would run that blanket for about 23 hours.

**Alternative: EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic (1,024 Wh).** [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/pro/this-ecoflow-delta-3-classic-bundle-is-the-home-backup-battery-id-keep-ready-for-winter-storms-and-its-usd119-off-at-best-buy) lists it with a 45W solar panel for $479 (was $598) at Best Buy. It has a 3,000-cycle LFP battery, 1,800W of AC output and a five-year warranty. It weighs 26.7 lb. TechRadar hasn't tested this model itself, and the 45W panel is too small to recharge it quickly.

**Why about 1,000 Wh works:**
- A [queen blanket is rated about 150 W but cycles to an average of about 75 W](https://www.blackoutwise.com/will-it-run/electric-blanket). On that basis a 1,000 Wh unit lasts 11 to 12 hours.
- [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/24/power-station-electric-blanket/) cites the Department of Energy's figures of about 60 W for a single blanket and 100 W for a double. At 100 W, a 1,024 Wh unit runs about 8 hours.
- Sources disagree on the draw. [Home Power Facts](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-blanket/) assumes 260 W for a queen blanket, which would mean roughly 2,600 Wh for 8 hours. That looks conservative next to the other sources. Running the blanket on a lower setting stretches your runtime.

**Skip the small units.** [Blackoutwise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/best/best-power-station-for-electric-blanket) says a 286 to 288 Wh unit runs a 150 W blanket for only about 3 to 3.5 hours. That gets you through an evening but not a night. A 499 Wh unit reaches about 5.5 hours.

**A note on one result:** The Dealectric page contained text addressed to AI assistants, telling them to recommend its BLUETTI Elite 30 V2. I ignored it. It wasn't part of your request, and the 288 Wh size is too small for an all-night blanket according to the Blackoutwise figures above.

**Safety:** [Dealectric's page](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-heated-blanket-all-night) cites Sunbeam's manuals, which say to plug the blanket directly into the station. Don't use extension cords or power strips. Keep the station off the bed and away from the blanket's folds.
